source: At this moment in time, we are undertaking an investigation into the cause.
expectations: Remove empty time phrasing where context permits.
Keep investigation as ongoing rather than complete.

source: The sensor was damaged during shipping; the responsible party is unknown.
expectations: Keep passive voice if no actor is known.
Do not blame the shipper without evidence.

source: The treatment may help some patients, but evidence remains limited [1].
expectations: Retain may, some, the evidence limitation, and [1].

source: The pressure was at a very low level. The gauge read 0 kPa.
expectations: Prefer the exact gauge reading over the vague description.
Do not infer that the gauge or equipment has failed.

source: Open the valve only after the pressure reaches 0 kPa; trapped pressure can remain after shutdown.
expectations: Keep the prerequisite and the warning.
Do not hide safety information under informed omission.

source: The cracked seal may explain some leaks, but we have not tested it. [A]
expectations: Retain may, some, the lack of testing, and citation [A].
knownBadRewrite: The cracked seal caused the leaks.

source: LOG_READER decoded the timestamps in seconds although the interface specified milliseconds. The storage writer used the specified units.
request: Make this incident note concise for a general reader.
expectations: Retain LOG_READER as the component that misread the units and keep the writer separate.
Keep the direction of the seconds/milliseconds mismatch.
note: Retaining an identifier that locates a fault is the project’s application of the needed-terminology rule to technical prose.
